text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- An 18-year-old unemployed Motswana woman has given birth to Siamese twins in the mining town of Jawaneng. The mother and her babies have been moved to Gaborone and it has been established they are joined at chest and abdomen and share one liver and heart. Hospital authorites say an operation to separate the twins is planned and would most likely take place in South Africa, but they believe the twins have only a slim chance of recovery.
- Minister of Agriculture Roy Blackbeard has indicated he will step down soon, but that he does not intend to immediately relinquish his parliamentary seat.

- The Botswana Bank Employees Union is to take the government to court to reverse a ruling that banks are essential services. Such categorisation limits the activity of the union because a long and elaborate procedure has to be followed before any industrial action can be initiated. The categorisation came after a spate of strikes in 1989.

- Botswana was among the first African countries to commit itself to democrcatic rule, but it is becoming the last to adopt a truly modern, enlightened and liberal democracy, says MMEGI in its comments on the draft Mass Media Communications Bill.
